mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns: a lower FEDFUNDS level (as of t-1mo) predicts positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (25th percentile), or rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 3.5% (as of t-1mo) signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 3.5%, or rank correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 3.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy combined with a weakening labor market, reducing equity valuations and leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0 and UNRATE > 3.5, or rank correlation between interaction signal and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery regime (HOUST > 1350), consumer spending and business investment are expected to rise, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1350, or rank correlation between HOUST and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 300.5 (as of t-1mo) signals persistent inflation that triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 300.5, or rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1350 thousand units and industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 102.5, it signals a robust economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1350 and INDPRO > 102.5, or rank correlation between interaction signal and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 returns: a higher PAYEMS level (as of t-1mo) predicts positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 150000 (75th percentile), or rank correlation between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below 100, it signals a supply shock or recession, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO is below 100, or rank correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over 3-year rolling window.
